error_reason: The planner correctly identified the approximate mass values for the subatomic particles but failed during the final comparison by incorrectly asserting that 10^-31 (electron) is greater than 10^-27 (proton) because 31 > 27, demonstrating a catastrophic misunderstanding of how negative exponents work. This arithmetic error directly inverted the logical conclusion, leading to the selection of the proton as the lightest particle instead of the correct answer, the electron.

hypotheses.rationale: The planner correctly identifies the mass values but performs a catastrophic logical error in the final comparison. It asserts that 10^-31 (electron) is greater than 10^-27 (proton) because 31 > 27, completely inverting the rules of exponents (negative powers). This fundamental arithmetic/logic error leads to the incorrect conclusion that the proton is the lightest, whereas the electron is actually the lightest. This is the decisive error as it is the first and only step shown, and it directly contradicts basic scientific facts.
